questions.q:
Statements (take them as true):
All pens are books.
All books are papers.
Conclusions:
I. All pens are papers.
II. All papers are pens.
Which of the following is correct?
o: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.e: Pens lie inside books, which lie inside papers, so all pens are papers. The reverse, all papers are pens, does not follow.

questions.q:
Statements (take them as true):
All cats are dogs.
No dog is a bird.
Conclusions:
I. No cat is a bird.
II. Some birds are cats.
Which of the following is correct?
o: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.e: Cats lie inside dogs, and dogs share nothing with birds, so no cat is a bird. The second conclusion contradicts this, so it is false.

questions.q:
Statements (take them as true):
Some doctors are teachers.
All teachers are singers.
Conclusions:
I. All doctors are singers.
II. Some singers are doctors.
Which of the following is correct?
o: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.e: The doctors who are teachers are also singers, so some singers are doctors. Only some doctors are teachers, so all doctors being singers is not certain.

questions.q:
Statements (take them as true):
No flower is a stone.
Some stones are rivers.
Conclusions:
I. No river is a flower.
II. Some rivers are not flowers.
Which of the following is correct?
o: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.e: The rivers that are stones cannot be flowers, so some rivers are not flowers. Other rivers might be flowers, so no river is a flower is not certain.

questions.q:
Statements (take them as true):
All tables are chairs.
Some chairs are beds.
Conclusions:
I. Some tables are beds.
II. Some beds are tables.
Which of the following is correct?
o: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.e: The beds that are chairs may or may not be tables, since tables form only one part of chairs. So no link between tables and beds follows.

questions.q:
Statements (take them as true):
Some wheels are tyres.
All tyres are rubber items.
Conclusions:
I. Some wheels are rubber items.
II. Some rubber items are tyres.
Which of the following is correct?
o: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.e: The wheels that are tyres are rubber items, so some wheels are rubber items. Those same tyres are rubber items, so some rubber items are tyres. Both follow.

questions.q:
Statements (take them as true):
Some books are novels.
Conclusions:
I. Some novels are books.
II. Some books are not novels.
Which of the following is correct?
o: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.e: A 'some' statement can be reversed, so some novels are books. But some books being novels says nothing about books that are not novels.

questions.q:
Statements (take them as true):
All horses are animals.
Some animals are wild things.
Conclusions:
I. Some horses are wild things.
II. No horse is a wild thing.
Which of the following is correct?
o: Either conclusion I or II follows
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.e: The wild animals may or may not be horses, so neither conclusion is certain by itself. They form a complementary pair, though: either some horses are wild or no horse is wild.

questions.q:
Statements (take them as true):
All pens are pencils.
Some pencils are sticks.
No stick is a ruler.
Conclusions:
I. Some pencils are not rulers.
II. Some pens are not rulers.
Which of the following is correct?
o: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.e: The pencils that are sticks cannot be rulers, so some pencils are not rulers. Those pencils need not be pens, so the pens conclusion does not follow.

questions.q:
Statements (take them as true):
Some cars are buses.
Some buses are trucks.
All trucks are vans.
Conclusions:
I. Some cars are vans.
II. Some buses are vans.
Which of the following is correct?
o: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.e: The buses that are trucks are vans, so some buses are vans. The cars that are buses need not be trucks, so a link between cars and vans does not follow.

questions.q:
Statements (take them as true):
All roses are flowers.
All lilies are flowers.
Conclusions:
I. All roses are lilies.
II. Some roses are lilies.
Which of the following is correct?
o: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.e: Roses and lilies are both inside flowers but may be separate. Therefore neither all roses being lilies nor some roses being lilies is certain.

questions.q:
Statements (take them as true):
No bag is a box.
Some trays are bags.
Conclusions:
I. Some trays are not boxes.
II. Some bags are trays.
Which of the following is correct?
o: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.e: The trays that are bags cannot be boxes, so some trays are not boxes. The same bags are trays, so some bags are trays. Both follow.

questions.q:
Statements (take them as true):
Some birds are kites.
All kites are toys.
No toy is a game.
Conclusions:
I. Some birds are toys.
II. Some birds are not games.
III. No kite is a game.
Which of the following is correct?
o: All of I, II and III follow
questions.e: The birds that are kites are toys, so some birds are toys, and those birds are not games. Kites lie inside toys, which share nothing with games, so no kite is a game. All three follow.

questions.q:
Statements (take them as true):
All shirts are cloths.
Some cloths are red things.
No red thing is a brick.
Conclusions:
I. Some cloths are not bricks.
II. Some shirts are red things.
III. No shirt is a brick.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.e: The cloths that are red cannot be bricks, so some cloths are not bricks. Shirts need not be red, and shirts could include bricks, so the other two do not follow.

questions.q:
Statements (take them as true):
All lamps are bulbs.
No bulb is a tube.
Conclusions:
I. Some lamps are tubes.
II. No lamp is a tube.
Which of the following is correct?
o: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.e: Lamps lie inside bulbs, and bulbs share nothing with tubes, so no lamp is a tube. Some lamps being tubes contradicts this.

questions.q:
Statements (take them as true):
All players are athletes.
Some athletes are coaches.
All coaches are winners.
Conclusions:
I. Some players are winners.
II. Some athletes are winners.
III. Some winners are athletes.
Which of the following is correct?
o: All of I, II and III follow
questions.e: Athletes who are coaches are winners, so some athletes are winners and some winners are athletes. Players need not be those coaches, so players being winners is not certain.

questions.q:
Statements (take them as true):
Some nets are ropes.
All ropes are wires.
No wire is a cable.
Conclusions:
I. All nets are wires.
II. No rope is a cable.
III. Some wires are nets.
Which of the following is correct?
o: All of I, II and III follow
questions.e: Ropes are wires and wires share nothing with cables, so no rope is a cable. The nets that are ropes are wires, so some wires are nets. Not every net need be a wire.

questions.q:
Statements (take them as true):
Some hens are ducks.
No duck is a goose.
All swans are geese.
Conclusions:
I. Some hens are not geese.
II. Some swans are hens.
III. No swan is a duck.
Which of the following is correct?
o: All of I, II and III follow
questions.e: The hens that are ducks cannot be geese, so some hens are not geese. Swans lie inside geese, which share nothing with ducks, so no swan is a duck. Some swans being hens is not certain.

questions.q:
Statements (take them as true):
No man is a worker.
Some clerks are men.
All managers are workers.
Conclusions:
I. Some clerks are not workers.
II. No clerk is a manager.
III. Some managers are men.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.e: The clerks who are men are not workers, so some clerks are not workers. Those clerks are not managers, but other clerks might be, so no clerk is a manager is not certain. Managers are workers, so none is a man.

questions.q:
Statements (take them as true):
All boys are students.
Some students are athletes.
All athletes are singers.
Conclusions:
I. Some boys are singers.
II. No boy is a singer.
Which of the following is correct?
o: Either conclusion I or II follows
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.e: The students who are athletes are singers, but boys may or may not be among them. So some boys being singers is not certain, nor is no boy being a singer; one of the two must be true.
